# nonException

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** an `Exception`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonException() — Checks whether a value is **not** an `Exception`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonException<T>(value: T | Exception): value is T;
```

`nonException(value)` is the same test as `!isException(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

The library's own hierarchy only. A plain `Error` does not qualify, which is exactly what makes the check useful in a `catch` block that has to tell the two apart.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type             | Description         |
| :-------- | :--------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| Exception` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not an `Exception`; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonException(new Error()); // => true
nonException({}); // => true
nonException(null); // => true
nonException(new IllegalArgumentException()); // => false
```
